record.paper_title: The Lieb-Thirring inequalities: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: In dimension d=1, determine the optimal constant L_{γ,1} for the remaining unresolved range 1/2 < γ < 3/2. Equivalently, decide whether Conjecture 12 is true there, namely whether L_{γ,1} equals the one-particle constant L^(1)_{γ,1} throughout that interval.

evidence.quote: In view of Theorem 13, Conjecture 12 is proved for γ = 1/2 and for γ ≥ 3/2. The case γ ∈ (1/2, 3/2) is open.
Dimension d = 1. Conjecture 12 is generally believed to be true. The only remaining case is the range 1/2 < γ < 3/2, where the optimal constant should be L(1)γ,1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For γ ≥ 0 and d ≥ 1, the Lieb–Thirring inequality asserts that there exists a finite constant L_{γ,d} such that, for every real-valued potential V on R^d with V_- = max(-V,0) ∈ L^{γ+d/2}(R^d), the negative eigenvalues λ_1(V) ≤ λ_2(V) ≤ … < 0 of the Schrödinger operator -Δ + V on L^2(R^d) satisfy

  ∑_j |λ_j(V)|^γ ≤ L_{γ,d} ∫_{R^d} V_-(x)^{γ+d/2} dx.

Let L_{γ,d} denote the smallest such constant (the optimal/sharp Lieb–Thirring constant). Define the one-particle constant L^{(1)}_{γ,d} as the value of the analogous ratio when V is restricted to potentials producing exactly one negative eigenvalue; explicitly,

  L^{(1)}_{γ,d} = sup_V |λ_1(V)|^γ / ∫_{R^d} V_-^{γ+d/2} dx,

with the supremum taken over nontrivial V for which -Δ + V has at least one negative eigenvalue. In dimension d = 1 it is known that L_{γ,1} = L^{(1)}_{γ,1} for γ = 1/2 and for all γ ≥ 3/2.

Problem. Determine the optimal constant L_{γ,1} for every γ in the open interval (1/2, 3/2). Equivalently, decide whether

  L_{γ,1} = L^{(1)}_{γ,1}    for all γ ∈ (1/2, 3/2).
artifact.status_search_result: The one-dimensional sharp Lieb–Thirring constant for γ ∈ (1/2, 3/2) remains an open problem. The endpoints γ = 1/2 (Hundertmark–Lieb–Thomas) and γ ≥ 3/2 (Lieb–Thirring; with d=1, γ=3/2 going back to Gardner–Greene–Kruskal–Miura giving L_{3/2,1}=3/16) are settled, but no proof or disproof of the conjectured equality L_{γ,1} = L^{(1)}_{γ,1} on the open interval has been published as of recent surveys (2022).

status_evidence.title: The state of the Lieb–Thirring conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Survey reviews known cases; identifies γ ∈ (1/2, 3/2) in d=1 as still open.
status_evidence.claim: The one-dimensional case for γ strictly between 1/2 and 3/2 is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the Lieb-Thirring constants L_{γ,1} for γ ≥ 1/2 (Hundertmark–Lieb–Thomas)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the sharp constant at γ=1/2 in dimension one.
status_evidence.claim: Endpoint γ=1/2 is solved with L_{1/2,1}=L^{(1)}_{1/2,1}.

status_evidence.title: Lieb–Thirring inequality — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: States the conjecture, the proven cases γ=1/2 and γ ≥ 3/2 in 1D, and lists intermediate γ as open.
status_evidence.claim: Status summary corroborates that 1/2 < γ < 3/2 in d=1 is open.
